safe staffing levels are not just a numbers game, they need to be able take account of the complexity of the work and the needs of those receiving care and their families.
there is no one agreed upon definition of what safe staffing levels for learning disability nurses are, and what they mean to patients and their relatives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between safe staffing levels and the delivery of quality compassionate nursing care.
how the learning disability nursing workforce is deployed to deliver safe, quality and compassionate nursing care.
the relationship between staffing and the delivery compassionate care, and the safety of patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the literature suggests that there is no one size fits all approach to safe staffing levels for learning disability nurses.
safe staffing levels in learning disability nursing are a complex concept and are influenced by a range of factors.
there is a need to better understand what the term'safe and compassionate staffing' really means, and how we can achieve it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evidence base for staffing levels in learning disability nursing is weak.
safe staffing is not simply about numbers.
there is a need for further work in the field of learning disability safe staffing levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to develop a clear definition of what safe staffing levels mean for people with learning disabilities, and their families.
there is a need for a national consensus on the definition of safe staffing and compassionate care.
